introduction.text: The Monument to Giordano Bruno in Rome commemorates the philosopher who was burned at the stake in 1600 and symbolizes the conflict between free thought and religious authority.

history.description: Giordano Bruno was executed by burning at the stake on 17 February 1600 at Campo de' Fiori in Rome.
Freemasons and anti-clerical groups planned and funded the monument between 1884 and 1888, culminating in its approval by the city council on 10 December 1888.
The monument was unveiled on 9 June 1889 at the site of Bruno's execution, drawing large crowds of freethinkers and provoking a strong reaction from the Catholic Church.
In 2008 a statue depicting Bruno's death was installed at Potsdamer Platz station in Berlin.

design.description: The monument was created by Grand Master Mason Ettore Ferrari and features a bronze statue of Giordano Bruno with an inscription and eight medallions of historical thinkers.

art.description: Eight medallions on the plinth depict Paolo Sarpi, Tommaso Campanella, Petrus Ramus, Lucilio Vanini, Aonio Paleario, Michele Serveto, John Wycliffe, and Jan Hus, all of whom challenged religious authority.
